A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-verbalization faithfulness study. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison despite the changed title, formatting and appendix numbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original feature-extraction, activation-inversion and PersonaQA experiments, including prompt-sensitivity and entity-resolution analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds experiments examining inversion-layer choice and Patchscopes execution order.

M1.justification: The verbalization, inversion and probing procedures remain unchanged. Cross-model affine mapping already appears in v3 Appendix F. The revised inversion-loss description agrees with the input-reconstruction procedure already detailed in v3, so it does not establish an objective change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same feature-extraction relations, LatentQA, MS MARCO, PersonaQA variants and entity-resolution tasks. The added layer and execution-order experiments vary configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same verbalization, zero-shot, inversion and logistic-probe comparators. The cross-model comparison already existed in v3 Table 14. Parallel versus linear dispatch varies the implementation setting of Patchscopes, without introducing another comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: v4 adds inversion training and evaluation at layer 7 with zero-shot interpretation, and linear-dispatch Patchscopes evaluation alongside the original parallel execution. Section 5.1 also newly says 'unseen personas', but the retained appendix protocol does not clearly document a corresponding split revision.

E4.justification: Appendices B.3 and D.6 add targeted checks of execution-order sensitivity and inversion-layer choice. Existing prompt perturbations, knowledge-swapping controls, zero-shot ensembling and entity-resolution analyses remain; their relocation or renumbering does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: McNemar's tests, Bonferroni correction and significance markings are retained, as is the control that ensembles outputs generated with different seeds. The new experiments report point accuracies without introducing repeated-run uncertainty estimates or new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports average Patchscopes accuracy of 0.38 for parallel execution and 0.49 for linear dispatch; Table 16 adds layer-7 inversion results. In v3 Table 14 versus v4 Table 2, the Llama3 LIT reference row changes, including food-country accuracy from 0.30 to 0.45. Its new values match Table 1's layer averages despite the single-layer caption, so a same-setting improvement is not established. Other matched results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version adds formal theory or proofs. v4's explicit activation-concatenation equation in Section 2 restates the operation already described in v3; it introduces no new mathematical definition or reasoning.

C1.justification: The central findings about benchmark shortcuts and verbalizers' own knowledge remain. v4 strengthens claimed novelty by explicitly claiming the first cross-family verbalization evaluation in Section 3's footnote 6 and the first investigation of verbalization faithfulness in Section 6.

C2.justification: v4 newly attributes execution-order differences to Patchscopes nondeterminism and contrasts this with trained verbalizers. It discusses layer-dependent input recovery and expands Section 8 with concrete evaluation proposals using exclusive knowledge, training-time cutoffs or disagreeing model responses. These extend the earlier interpretations and recommendations.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the future code-release placeholder with specific code and dataset access information. Appendix B discloses parallel versus linear execution, explicitly clarifies reuse of the layer-15-trained verbalizer across layers, and corrects execution accounting from 3072 to 2880 runs. Most hyperparameters, hardware details and resource estimates are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds DecoderLens by Langedijk et al. (2024), removes Lost in Embeddings by Li et al. (2025), and makes explicit priority claims about cross-family evaluation and faithfulness analysis. LatentQA's change from a 2024 preprint citation to its 2026 publication identifies the same work.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes extensive language editing, including a shorter title, rewritten introductory contributions and experimental explanations, and expanded limitations and conclusions. Introductory bullets become paragraphs, an Impact Statement is added, training and GPU appendices are combined, and cross-model discussion is integrated into the main text.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Figure 2's panels are stacked, Figures 1 and 3 clarify parametric-knowledge labels, the cross-model table moves into the main text, two experimental tables are added, and former Tables 5 and 6 are transposed. The prompt-sensitivity plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new layer-choice and execution-order checks, clarified reconstruction-training description, and concrete code/data access information modestly improve transparency and reproducibility. These benefits are limited by Table 2's ambiguous LIT aggregation and Appendix B.3's insufficiently supported attribution of execution differences to nondeterminism. Most main results and the central empirical argument remain unchanged.
